subject: EchoHealth POC: success metrics, guardrails & ops onboarding
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@echohealth.com>, Engineering Team <eng@echohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: EchoHealth POC: success metrics, guardrails & ops onboarding

Hi Alice — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have a single place to track:

Call summary:
- Goal: validate Redwood Inference as the inference backbone for EchoHealth’s clinical QA assistant. Primary concerns: latency, cost, throughput at peak, and PHI-safe handling.
- Scope for POC: 3-week technical evaluation using a neutral dataset + a small sample of de-identified clinical prompts you provide. Not an ingress of PHI until we confirm controls.

Proposed success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 180 ms for 512-token responses (target; stretch 150 ms).
- Throughput: sustain 40 concurrent inference requests with 95% success rate; equivalent to ~800 tokens/sec in our baseline harness.
- Cost: effective cost <= $0.40 per 1k tokens for the evaluated workload (includes batching and KV cache gains).
- Quality: accuracy/utility measured by your evaluation set — target NPS-style scorer >= 4.0/5 and pass-rate >= 88% on the prioritized prompt set.
- Reliability: zero customer-impacting errors during scheduled smoke tests; graceful fallback to smaller model under load.

Operational guardrails / tasks:
1) Data handling & security: we will operate in a private VPC for the trial. Compliance contact: we will not accept PHI until a short SNDS/controls checklist is completed by your compliance team.
2) Integration: Ben (cc’d) will own the technical integration and instrument the latency/throughput tests.
3) Monitoring: we’ll provide a dashboard with token-level cost, p95 latency, error rate, and sample output diffing for quality regression checks.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (next week): kick-off + access provisioning (credentials + VPC).
- Week 1: smoke tests + baseline benchmark run.
- Week 2: quality evaluation on your prompt set + tuning (batching, quantization suggestions).
- Week 3: readout + handoff and recommendation (go/no-go).

Attachments: EchoHealth-POC-Success-Metrics-Template.xlsx (attached) — fills the KPI cells we discussed.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Alice: confirm the 3-week cadence and whether compliance can review the controls checklist by Monday EOD.
- Engineering: share a single example endpoint and an on-call contact for the integration window.
- Ben: will draft the runbook and a baseline benchmark script; Hannah will own scheduling.

Thanks — I’ll schedule the kickoff for Tuesday morning unless you prefer a different slot.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com]

[Attachment: EchoHealth-POC-Success-Metrics-Template.xlsx]
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@echohealth.com>

Date: Fri, 15 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EchoHealth POC: success metrics, guardrails & ops onboarding

Thanks Hannah — this is very helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. A few notes from our side:

- Latency: our internal product goal is p95 <= 150 ms for short clinical prompts; can Redwood run a stretch configuration so we can see both baseline and optimized numbers?
- Cost: target cost of $0.35 / 1k tokens would be preferable; we understand this depends on quantization and batching.
- PHI: compliance is looped (cc). They will need the controls checklist and a short architecture diagram before we hand over any de-identified data.

We can do the kickoff on Tuesday 2027-04-20 09:00 PT if that works. Engineering will provide an integration contact (I’ll share the endpoint + API key for a sandbox) by end of day Monday.

Attaching our internal evaluation rubric separately (will send via Drive link).

-Alice
Product Lead, EchoHealth
alice.moreno@echohealth.com

- For the 150 ms stretch target, we’ll include a low-latency config and note any trade-offs to cost or throughput.
- Integration runbook: I’m attaching integration-runbook-v1.0.pdf (stub) — will include steps for VPC peering, credentials rotation, and a small smoke test suite.

- Legal/Compliance: Hannah — please send the lightweight controls checklist and architecture diagram to EchoHealth compliance. I’ll standby to escalate if they request an on-site audit or additional evidence.
- Deal tracker: I’ve created the HubSpot record HSP-83421 and linked the Drive folder. I’ll also schedule a 30-minute readout for the week after the POC completes.
